wareworks.ponder.bays_in_an_aisle.header: Rack Bays in a Warehouse Aisle
wareworks.ponder.bays_in_an_aisle.text_1: Two rack bays with no warehouse anywhere near them, one of them filled by hand
wareworks.ponder.bays_in_an_aisle.text_2: Lay the rails of an aisle in front of them and every bay becomes an addressable storage location
wareworks.ponder.bays_in_an_aisle.text_3: What a bay already held by hand is counted the moment the warehouse reaches it
wareworks.ponder.bays_in_an_aisle.text_4: There is no interface in front of a bay and nothing behind it: a fifty-bay wall is fifty blocks
wareworks.ponder.bays_in_an_aisle.text_5: The crane reaches in through the open front of the bay, as it does through an interface's slot
wareworks.ponder.bays_in_an_aisle.text_6: The filter slot says what belongs here; hold Right-Click on it with an empty hand to set a priority: higher fills first
wareworks.ponder.bays_in_an_aisle.text_7: And a Funnel, a Chute, a Belt or a Hopper fills a bay directly, which no other location allows
wareworks.ponder.bays_in_an_aisle.text_8: A chest behind an interface stays the right answer for the items you only own three of
wareworks.ponder.bays_in_an_aisle.text_9: Both kinds of storage live in one aisle: a bay for bulk goods, an interface for the long tail
wareworks.ponder.fluid_bay.text_1: A Fluid Bay is a storage location that is a tank: one fluid, and 64 buckets of it in copper
wareworks.ponder.fluid_bay.text_10: A Funnel, a Chute, a Belt or a Hopper cannot fill one: it would keep your empty bucket
wareworks.ponder.fluid_bay.text_11: And breaking a bay loses whatever is in it, as breaking any tank does: pump it out first
wareworks.ponder.fluid_bay.text_12: The empty bay comes back, and the goggles and the first hit warn you while it holds anything
wareworks.ponder.fluid_bay.text_2: A bucket in your hand works both ways, and the level you see is the whole readout
wareworks.ponder.fluid_bay.text_3: Create's pipes reach every face but the one towards the aisle, and a pump fills a whole bay
wareworks.ponder.fluid_bay.text_4: In a warehouse aisle it is an ordinary storage location with its own address and priority
wareworks.ponder.fluid_bay.text_5: Its filter is a fluid: click the slot with a filled bucket and that fluid belongs here
wareworks.ponder.fluid_bay.text_6: Put a bucket of lava into a warehouse input and the crane carries the whole container to it
wareworks.ponder.fluid_bay.text_7: The bay drains the whole bucket, and the crane is left holding the empty one
wareworks.ponder.fluid_bay.text_8: The empty bucket is then shelved as ordinary stock, in a rack bay or a chest
wareworks.ponder.fluid_bay.text_9: So the warehouse holds lava as a fluid and the bucket as stock, and counts both
wareworks.ponder.fluid_request.text_1: With a Fluid Bay in the aisle, the terminal lists each fluid as a row of its own above the items
wareworks.ponder.fluid_request.text_2: Click it for buckets of that fluid: the terminal first says which containers it uses and how many trips that takes
wareworks.ponder.fluid_request.text_3: The crane takes an empty container from stock, the largest first: here an empty bucket
wareworks.ponder.fluid_request.text_4: The bay fills it, and the crane carries the filled bucket straight on to the terminal
wareworks.ponder.fluid_request.text_5: and drops it into the terminal: one filled bucket per trip, which is why the question counts the trips
wareworks.ponder.fluid_request.text_6: With no empty container in stock the row turns red, and if a pattern makes buckets, the terminal offers to have them made first
wareworks.ponder.fluid_request.text_7: For bulk, a pipe at the back of the bay draws the fluid off without any container
wareworks.ponder.hand_truck.header: Carrying Containers with the Hand Truck
wareworks.ponder.hand_truck.text_1: Right-Click a Chest or a Barrel with an empty Hand Truck
wareworks.ponder.hand_truck.text_2: The container goes onto the truck with everything inside it
wareworks.ponder.hand_truck.text_3: While it is loaded you walk slowly, cannot sprint and cannot glide with an Elytra
wareworks.ponder.hand_truck.text_4: Right-Click the ground to set it down again, facing you, with exactly what it held
wareworks.ponder.hand_truck.text_5: A loaded truck fits into no other container and cannot be dropped; warehouse blocks cannot be carried
wareworks.ponder.rack_bay.header: Storing Bulk Goods in a Rack Bay
wareworks.ponder.rack_bay.text_1: A Rack Bay is a storage location in a single block: nothing in front of it, nothing behind it
wareworks.ponder.rack_bay.text_10: Breaking a full bay resets it: the empty bay comes back and its load stays in the world
wareworks.ponder.rack_bay.text_11: However much was inside, it lands on one Pallet, with the item and the count written above it
wareworks.ponder.rack_bay.text_12: You refill by hand with the bay's own gesture, and a Pallet cannot be picked up or carried away
wareworks.ponder.rack_bay.text_13: A plain Hopper drains a Pallet, and a Deployer can; Create's Belts, Chutes and Funnels cannot
wareworks.ponder.rack_bay.text_2: It holds one item type and a great deal of it: 64 stacks in a wooden bay
wareworks.ponder.rack_bay.text_3: Right-Click with an item and one goes in; even the first item already shows on the front
wareworks.ponder.rack_bay.text_4: Hold Shift and a whole stack goes in at once
wareworks.ponder.rack_bay.text_5: An empty hand takes items back out: one of them, or a stack with Shift
wareworks.ponder.rack_bay.text_6: The load on the pallet grows as the bay fills, so you read how full it is by walking past
wareworks.ponder.rack_bay.text_7: Goggles read out the exact count, the capacity and the material the bay is built from
wareworks.ponder.rack_bay.text_8: A second item type is refused: a bay with no filter keeps the first type that arrived in it
wareworks.ponder.rack_bay.text_9: Empty it and it forgets again, so you can put up a wall of bays and let it fill itself
wareworks.ponder.rack_wall.text_1: Set bays beside each other and a rack wall grows; a click on the side of one copies its direction
wareworks.ponder.rack_wall.text_2: They stack as high as you like; the crane's Mast Height is what decides how far up it reaches
wareworks.ponder.rack_wall.text_3: The material decides how much one bay holds: 64 stacks of wood, 256 of andesite, 1,024 of brass
wareworks.ponder.rack_wall.text_4: But a bay may carry nothing stronger above it: a brass bay on top of wood is refused outright
wareworks.ponder.rack_wall.text_5: The rack underneath would give way, so the strong material goes low and a wall is upgraded bottom up
wareworks.ponder.rack_wall.text_6: A command or a schematic can still build the wrong column, and every bay underneath says so in gold
wareworks.ponder.rack_wall.text_7: They keep every item and the crane still fetches from them; the warehouse only stores nothing there
wareworks.ponder.shared.crane_needs_rota: Stacker Cranes need Rotational Force from below
Moving Items with a Stacker Crane
Stacker Cranes store and retrieve items in a warehouse aisle
An aisle is one straight run of Warehouse Rails; a warehouse may have several
Storage sits on both sides of the aisle, on as many levels as the crane can reach
A Warehouse Controller behind the dock keeps the stock and plans every job
Faster rotation moves it faster; without rotation it pauses where it is
It travels along the rails and lifts its carriage to the right level
Then its telescopic arm reaches into the rack and the grabber moves the items
The Mast Height on the dock sets how many levels the crane can reach
wareworks.ponder.tag.warehouse.descripti: Components which store and retrieve items with Stacker Cranes
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_corner.text_1: A warehouse is the Warehouse Rails in front of a Stacker Crane's dock
A Wrench closes a rail: it belongs to no warehouse, which keeps two of them apart and sends a stray rail away
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_corner.text_2: Rails connect wherever they touch, not only in a straight line
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_corner.text_3: Two rails at right angles turn the block they share into a corner
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_corner.text_4: Every straight run is one aisle: the one at the dock is A, the next one B
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_corner.text_5: The machine rolls onto that block, swings a quarter turn and drives on down the next aisle
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_corner.text_6: So items reach every aisle of the warehouse, and one block can collect them all
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_corner.text_7: A rack in the corner works too: it belongs to the aisle it faces away from
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_corner.text_8: It reaches both from the very same block, a quarter turn apart
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_corner.text_9: Its address says which: A-01-05L on aisle A, B-01-00L on aisle B
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_crafter_feede: A Crafter Feeder goes on the back of a Warehouse Production and needs rotation
A vanilla Crafter stands in front of it, with a Warehouse Input in front of the Crafter's output
The station's patterns must be real crafting recipes, with exactly 1 item in each cell
Order torches, and the crane brings the coal and the sticks to the station
The feeder lays them into the Crafter as the pattern shows them, and pulses it once per run
The torches go into the Warehouse Input, and the crane stores them like any other item
A pattern that is no crafting recipe is shown red in the station and is never fetched
Wareworks still crafts nothing itself: the Crafter does
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_filters.text_: Every storage location has a filter slot on its aisle side
An empty slot accepts everything, which is how every warehouse starts
Click it with an item, and only that item is stored here
List, attribute and package filters work the same way
Dedicated locations fill before any unfiltered one
Changing a filter moves nothing, and what is inside can always be retrieved
An item that matches no filter needs a location without one
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_interface.tex: Any inventory beside the aisle can become a storage location
A Warehouse Interface in front of it turns it into one
Its brass port faces the inventory, its framed plate with the arm slot faces the aisle
Together with the crane's aisle, every location gets an address: aisle letter, level and position
Goggles show that address, the attached inventory and what it stores
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_junction.head: Rails That Split
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_junction.text: One straight run of Warehouse Rails in front of the dock is one aisle
The brass port decides, exactly as in a corner: a rack belongs to the aisle it faces away from
Their addresses say which: A-01-06R on aisle A, C-01-01R on aisle C
Rails may leave that run sideways, in the middle of it and not only at its end
Three rails meet on the block they share: it is a junction, and a position of both aisles
As many side aisles as you like may join the same run
A straight run stays one aisle through every junction, so all of this is aisle A
Every side aisle is one of its own, counted outwards from its junction: B and C
At a junction the machine picks its way: straight over it, or round the bend
So goods from every aisle of the warehouse reach the one block you collect them at
These two racks are twins: each one stands beside the run and beside aisle C at once
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_ordering_to_a: A requesting Warehouse Output with a Create Packager at its back is a package door
The sign on the Packager names the door, and is the address on every box it sends
In the terminal's screen, a button left of your inventory chooses where a click delivers
Click it for the next door: its name turns gold, and a click on an item now goes there
The crane carries the goods into the door, never more than its port can take
Your own redstone fires the Packager, and the box leaves with the sign's address
Clipboard lists and the ingredients the crafting grid fetches always come to the terminal
Each time the screen opens it starts on Here again, so clicks come to the terminal
A Stock Link on the Packager makes it ignore redstone: the door is red and cannot be chosen
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_packages_at_t: A Create Packager behind a Warehouse Output packs whatever the warehouse hands over
Whatever address it carries: the warehouse keeps what was inside and the box is gone
A package is opened whole or not at all, so the input needs room for every stack in it
Engineer's Goggles on either door say what it is doing, and why a package was refused
Its back has to touch the station, and which station that is decides the direction
A port only ever hands items out, so a Packager there can only pack: it cannot be set wrong
A plain sign on the Packager is the address every box it sends will carry
A Smart Observer over the port powers the Packager while anything is waiting there
The crane brings what the port asked for, and the Packager boxes it up
One box holds up to nine stacks, and a door sends about one box a second
A funnel, a chute or a Frogport takes the box from the Packager and sends it on its way
The same Packager at a Warehouse Input is an in door: it takes arriving packages apart
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_port_acceptin: Hold Right-Click on a Warehouse Output with a Wrench, and it accepts items instead of asking
It turns andesite where the crane reaches in, and shows its rank on the back you wire up
A negative rank ranks it after every storage location, so it only gets what cannot be kept
A stock rule's maximum is what makes one necessary: above it no location takes the item
The surplus then leaves through the port instead of backing the input up
Nothing is destroyed: what you build behind the port decides where the items go
Unless powered it needs no wiring at all, and one lever switches the overflow off
A positive rank makes it a diversion instead: then it takes items before they are stored
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_port_collecti: A machine drops its result into a chest of its own, and nothing takes it from there
The Collect row of its board turns the port around: now the warehouse fetches instead of waiting
Copper where the crane reaches in says so, and the port reads the inventory right behind it
The crane reaches through the port into that inventory and stores what it finds
That closes the loop: the crane brings the ingredients and takes the product back
Its filter decides what is fetched at all; without one it takes whatever that side hands out
A port collects only while the warehouse may still store: at a maximum it stops by itself
Unless powered it needs no wiring at all, and one lever stops the fetching
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_port_requesti: Supplying a Machine from a Warehouse
A Warehouse Output asks the warehouse for the item in its filter slot
Hold Right-Click on that slot to set the amount, and on the rows when the port acts
On a pulse it asks once per signal, and the crane brings that one load
While powered it asks again by itself as soon as the last items have arrived
Never more than one trip at a time, so a machine behind it stays supplied without a clock
Switching the signal off stops the next trip; what is already on its way still arrives
Unless powered turns that around: the port then works unwired, and a lever switches it off
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_production.te: A Warehouse Production feeds the machines you build next to it
Its pattern only says what one run of your machine needs and makes; nothing is used up
A terminal offers that result even when the warehouse holds none of it
The controller reserves the ingredients and the crane brings them to the station
Your own funnel, chute, belt or Mechanical Arm carries them into the machine
Wareworks delivers and collects; it never crafts anything itself
The product comes back through an ordinary Warehouse Input, like any other item
The crane stores it, and your waiting request is served from that stock
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_production_ch: A button takes two machines, and this warehouse holds nothing but logs
The buttons come back the same way, and the crane brings them to the terminal
If an ingredient is missing and nothing can make it, the click is refused and names it
The warehouse orders your machines one after the other; it never crafts anything itself
Order the button at a terminal anyway: your patterns can reach it
That one click plans the whole chain: one production order per step, at your own stations
The first step gets its ingredients; the step waiting for it is given nothing at all
Your own funnel, chute, belt or Mechanical Arm carries them into the machine
The planks come back through an ordinary Warehouse Input, like any other item
They are stored in a rack: what a step makes is ordinary stock, not a hand-over
Only now is the second step given its ingredients, out of that rack
and your second machine makes what you ordered
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_requesting.te: Right-click the screen to open the terminal; sneak to place a block against it
It lists everything the warehouse holds, and the search box finds an item by name
Click an item for the amount in the field, Shift for a stack, Ctrl for everything
Clicking the same item again grows the open request instead of starting a second trip
The crane fetches the items from the locations that hold them
and drops them into the terminal's own slots
Funnels, chutes, hoppers and Mechanical Arms can pull them out from there
Or put a clipboard in: the whole list is fetched, and each entry ticked off as it arrives
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_restocking.te: The warehouse holds fewer than a rule's minimum, and a station here has a pattern for it
So the warehouse orders it by itself: the same production order, with nobody asking for it
Never out of a reserve: with no ingredients it may spend, the rule waits and says so
Your own machine makes the product, exactly as it does for an order of yours
The product returns through an ordinary Warehouse Input, like any other item
An ordinary job stores it, the minimum is met again and the lamp goes out
If a machine swallows a batch and nothing comes back, that rule stops ordering
Check your machine, then click the rule's mark to let it order again
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_retrieving.te: Items leave a warehouse through a Warehouse Output
Click its filter slot with the item you want
Hold Right-Click on it to set the amount, at most one stack
Every redstone pulse asks the controller for that amount
The crane fetches the items from the location that holds them
and drops them into the output, where funnels, chutes, hoppers and Mechanical Arms pull them out
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_stock_rules.t: A Warehouse Stock Keeper holds the stock rules of its aisle
One row is one item and three numbers, and each number governs a different direction
The minimum is what comes in: below it a comparator on the keeper calls for the item
A farm of yours then runs exactly as long as the warehouse needs it
The maximum is what may be stored: above it the crane stops accepting the item
A Warehouse Input then backs up on purpose: that is the rule working, not a jam
The reserve is what may go out to automation: a redstone request stops at the last items
Only what is above it is fetched; the last ones stay in the rack
You are never stopped: a terminal serves you down to the last one and asks before it does
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_storing.text_: Items enter a warehouse through a Warehouse Input
Belts, funnels, chutes, hoppers and Mechanical Arms can put items in; nothing comes back out
The Warehouse Controller looks for a free storage location and orders a job
The crane drives to the input and its grabber takes the items
It carries them to the chosen location and puts them into the inventory behind it
While free locations are left, every item type gets one of its own
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_terminal.head: Placing a Warehouse Terminal
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_terminal.text: A Warehouse Terminal is placed with its screen facing you
Placed from beside the rack, the controller turns its arm port onto the aisle by itself
Stand where you want to read it: the screen keeps its face, only the port moves
A Wrench turns the screen to the next face, never onto the port, and off the aisle side
Goggles show its address, what was delivered here and why a request was refused
wareworks.production.nothing_stopped: Nothing this station makes is stopped
wareworks.production.resume_hint: Sneak-click the station to make them again
wareworks.production.resumed_lost: The warehouse makes %1$s again; %2$s ingredient items were delivered and never came back
wareworks.rail.closed: Rail closed: no warehouse runs through it any more
wareworks.rail.opened: Rail opened: it joins the rails it touches again
